data.gender_notes: Balvant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Balvant is derived from Sanskrit roots 'bal' meaning power and 'van' meaning to go or to protect. This name signifies a powerful and brave individual who is victorious in all aspects of life. The name Balvant carries the meaning “Powerful, Brave, Victorious” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Balvant usually hope their child will grow to embody powerful, brave, victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodying the spirit of courage and strength.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balvant total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Balvant carries a sense of strength, courage, and invincibility within the Indian cultural context. It is historically associated with warrior monarchs, brave soldiers, and religious sages throughout ancient Indian history. The name is reminiscent of legendary figures like Bhim (from the Mahabharat), who embodied power and strength.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, the name 'Balvant' has profound significance as it signifies an individual who is spiritually invincible, drawing strength from the divine to overcome all challenges in life. Through his power, he can protect not only himself but others as well. The name is a reminder of the divine presence within, inspiring the bearer to seek strength from the divine and act selflessly.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Balvant: Meaning 'one who has a strong and powerful mind'. In Hinduism, the name symbolizes strength, resilience, and the power of the mind over matter.

historical_references.reference: Balvant was a king of Malwa in central India during the late 12th and early 13th centuries. He was a powerful and able ruler who extended his kingdom's borders and maintained stability during a time of political turmoil.
historical_references.context: Malwa, central India, king and ruler

historical_references.reference: Balvant was also known as Bhoja II and was the second ruler of the Paramara dynasty in Malwa. He is remembered for his patronage of art, literature, and architecture, particularly the construction of the magnificent temple complex at Ekamra Keshara.
historical_references.context: Malwa, central India, Paramara dynasty, patron of art, literature, and architecture
